title: Nectarine frangipane tart
subtitle: shortcrust pastry filled with almond cream and topped with sliced nectarines
excerpt: Nectarine frangipane tart has a crisp, blind-baked shortcrust shell filled with almond frangipane and topped with nectarines cut into thin slices. The frangipane puffs up around the fruit as it bakes, setting into a moist, almond-scented filling. The tart is best eaten on the day it is made, warm or at room temperature.
sourceNotes: Frangipane as a pastry filling is named after the Marquis Muzio Frangipani, though the cream-based almond filling has French origins and was widely used in French patisserie from the seventeenth century. The combination with stone fruit such as nectarines and apricots became popular in British baking from the 1970s.

glossaryTerms.definition: An almond-based cream made from butter, sugar, eggs, and ground almonds, used as a filling for tarts and pastries. It sets firm when baked and has a moist, dense crumb.
Baking a pastry shell without filling, using baking paper and beans to keep the base flat and the sides upright. Used before adding a wet or cold filling.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The pastry case can be blind-baked the day before and stored at room temperature. Assemble and bake the tart on the day.

content.text: Nectarine frangipane tart is a crisp pastry case filled with almond
and topped with nectarine slices before baking. The frangipane puffs up around the fruit as it bakes, setting into a moist almond filling. The pastry shell is
first so it has a head start on the filling and does not go soggy underneath.

Make the pastry: rub the cold butter into the flour and icing sugar until the mixture resembles breadcrumbs. Add the egg yolk and enough cold water to bring the dough together. Press into a flat disc, wrap, and chill for 30 minutes.
Roll the pastry to about 3 mm on a lightly floured surface. Line a 23 cm loose-bottomed tart tin, pressing into the sides. Trim the edges. Chill for 15 minutes.

Heat the oven to 200 degrees C (fan 180 degrees C / gas 6). Line the pastry case with baking paper and fill with baking beans. Blind bake for 15 minutes, then remove the beans and paper and bake for a further 5 minutes until the base is set and pale. Cool slightly. Reduce the oven to 180 degrees C (fan 160 degrees C / gas 4).
Make the frangipane: beat the softened butter and caster sugar until light and fluffy. Beat in the eggs one at a time. Fold in the ground almonds and flour.
Spread the frangipane into the cooled pastry case. Arrange the nectarine slices overlapping across the surface, pressing them lightly into the frangipane.

Bake at 180 degrees C for 30 to 35 minutes until the frangipane is set and pale golden, and a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean. Cool in the tin for 20 minutes before unmoulding. Brush with warmed apricot jam to glaze if using.

attrs.problem: Pastry base soft and undercooked with the filling on top
attrs.avoid: Avoid skipping the blind bake; wet frangipane will not cook the raw pastry base in the time the filling takes.
attrs.fix: Blind bake the case fully, until the base is dry and just set, before adding the frangipane. The case should no longer look raw.

attrs.problem: Frangipane sinking and the fruit dropping through
attrs.avoid: Avoid over-softened or over-beaten frangipane; it becomes too loose to hold the fruit.
attrs.fix: Beat the butter and sugar only until just combined and fluffy. The frangipane should hold a thick ribbon when dropped from the spoon before going into the case.
